```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(psych) # Omega
library(lavaan) # CFA analysis
library(mirt) # IRT analysis
library(ggplot2)
library(ggiraph) # interactive plot
library(corrplot) #corrplot
library(htmlwidgets) # interaction online
```

```{r}
data = read.csv("International_vaiak.csv")
```

# Art Knowledge

```{r}
data_ak = data %>%
  filter(
    if_any(B1_Numeric:B6_Numeric, ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
  mutate(
    Expertise = factor(ArtExp_Expertise_cluster))

data_ak_original = data %>%
  filter(Sett_Version == "VAIAK") %>%
  filter(
    if_any(B1_Numeric:B6_Numeric, ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
  mutate(
    Expertise = factor(ArtExp_Expertise_cluster))

data_ak_revised = data %>%
  filter(Sett_Version == "VAIAK-R") %>%
  filter(
    if_any(B1_Numeric:B6_Numeric, ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
  mutate(
    Expertise = factor(ArtExp_Expertise_cluster))

data_ak_na = data %>%
  filter(is.na(Sett_Version)) %>%
  filter(
    if_any(B1_Numeric:B6_Numeric, ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
  mutate(
    Expertise = factor(ArtExp_Expertise_cluster))

write.csv(data_ak_na, "C:\\Users\\matte\\Desktop\\dataset_check_2.csv")
```

This graph represent the distribution of the score of the AK scale

```{r}

data_ak_score = data_ak %>%
  count(Art_Knowledge, name = "n") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Art_Knowledge))

graph_ak = ggplot(data_ak_score, aes(y = n, x = Art_Knowledge,
                                tooltip = paste0(Art_Knowledge, ": ", n), 
                                data_id = Art_Knowledge)) +
  geom_col_interactive(fill = "grey70",
                        hover_css = "fill:#009b64; 
                       stroke:black; 
                       stroke-width:1.5px;") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Variable : Art Interest distribution")  +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none")

girafe(ggobj = graph_ak) 
```

## Internal reliability

```{r, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
omega_ak = data_ak %>%                              # Omega analysis Art Knowledge
  select(starts_with("C") | starts_with("B")) %>%
  select(ends_with("Numeric")) %>%
  select(!ends_with("b_Numeric")) %>%
  omega
```

The McDonald's omega indicate a good internal reliability

```{r}
omega_ak$omega.tot
```

## Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA)

### One factor model

```{r}
Model_AK_one = "knowledge  =~ B1_Numeric + B2_Numeric + B3_Numeric + B4_Numeric + B5_Numeric + B6_Numeric +
                            C1_1_Numeric + C1_2_Numeric + C2_1_Numeric + C2_2_Numeric + C3_1_Numeric +
                            C3_2_Numeric + C4_1_Numeric + C4_2_Numeric + C5_1_Numeric + C5_2_Numeric +
                            C6_1_Numeric + C6_2_Numeric + C7_1_Numeric + C7_2_Numeric + C8_1_Numeric +
                            C8_2_Numeric + C9_1_Numeric + C9_2_Numeric + C10_1_Numeric + C10_2_Numeric

                            C1_1_Numeric ~~ C1_2_Numeric
                            C2_1_Numeric ~~ C2_2_Numeric
                            C3_1_Numeric ~~ C3_2_Numeric
                            C4_1_Numeric ~~ C4_2_Numeric
                            C5_1_Numeric ~~ C5_2_Numeric
                            C6_1_Numeric ~~ C6_2_Numeric
                            C7_1_Numeric ~~ C7_2_Numeric
                            C8_1_Numeric ~~ C8_2_Numeric
                            C9_1_Numeric ~~ C9_2_Numeric
                            C10_1_Numeric ~~ C10_2_Numeric" # model

AK_onefactor = cfa(Model_AK_one, data = data_ak, std.lv=TRUE, estimator = "WLSMV",   
                   ordered = names(data_ak %>% select(ends_with("Numeric") & !ends_with("b_Numeric"))))  

fitMeasures(AK_onefactor, c(
  "chisq",
  "df",
  "pvalue",
  "cfi",
  "tli",
  "rmsea",
  "rmsea.ci.lower",
  "rmsea.ci.upper",
  "rmsea.pvalue",
  "srmr"))    # Indices
```

```{r}
residuals = residuals(AK_onefactor, type = "cor") # residuals

residuals = residuals$cov

corrplot(residuals,
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         col.lim = c(-0.8, 0.8))  # Indices
```

## Item Responce Theory

### Full scale results

The Part B and C of the analysis are going to be run using different models.

```{r}
AK_joint = data_ak %>%
  select(ends_with("Numeric") & !ends_with("b_Numeric")) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

item_types = c(
  rep("3PL", 6),
  rep("2PL", 20))

model_joint = mirt.model("
  F1 = 1-26 
  START = (1-6, g, 0.25)
  FIXED = (1-6, g)") # F1 is the common factor

AK_joint_IRT = mirt(
  AK_joint,
  model_joint,
  itemtype = item_types)

data_ak %>%
  group_by(Expertise) %>%
  select("B4") %>%
  table() %>%
  barplot()

data_ak %>%
  group_by(Expertise) %>%
  select("B4_Numeric") %>%
  table() %>%
  barplot()

AK_joint %>%
  select("B4_Numeric") %>%
  table() %>%
  barplot()

AK_joint %>%
  select("B3_Numeric") %>%
  table() %>%
  barplot()

plot(AK_joint_IRT, type = "trace", 
     facet_items = TRUE) # ICCs and category functioning

summary(AK_joint_IRT) # threshold check
```

The Part B and C of the analysis are going to be run using different models.

### NA

```{r}
AK_joint = data_ak_na %>%
  select(ends_with("Numeric") & !ends_with("b_Numeric")) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

item_types = c(
  rep("3PL", 6),
  rep("2PL", 20))

model_joint = mirt.model("
  F1 = 1-26 
  START = (1-6, g, 0.25)
  FIXED = (1-6, g)") # F1 is the common factor

AK_joint_IRT = mirt(
  AK_joint,
  model_joint,
  itemtype = item_types)

data_ak_na %>%
  group_by(Expertise) %>%
  select("B4_Numeric") %>%
```

We can notice that it is in general pretty normally distributed around 0, with a limited skewness into the lower values.
